items.english: "Why are you so quiet?" the man said, looking with a sudden puzzlement at the woman's face. She hurriedly tried to say something, but unable to put anything into a single word she fell silent, and again her eyes went far away. And she saw the phantom-like picture again. Then for the first time she quietly heard the sound of the storm outside the door. She said nothing.
notes: Kept p19 and p21 questions identical as 'Why are you so quiet?' though Japanese varies doushite / naze, per bible. Kept 'far away', 'phantom-like picture', and storm heard quietly and literally.

items.english: Yes. There was that day. There was the day when all would turn to fond remembrance and forgiveness and peace. After a long life, and after long sorrow, and after long suffering, on the day after those days, there would be that peaceful day of fond remembrance and forgiveness. What were the suffering and sorrow of each single day. What were the tiredness and trouble of each single day. Before she knew it she had a smile on her face.
notes: Kept 'that day' unresolved and trio as 'fond remembrance and forgiveness and peace'. Kept threefold 'long' and 'each single day' repetitions flat; did not conclude or console.

items.english: "Why are you so quiet?" the man said again. She lifted her head as if startled, smiling fondly, "It has really been only a little while, hasn't it, since we married," she said, as if asking him too to remember all sorts of things, even the happy things from before their marriage.
notes: Grouped p21-p23 as one English paragraph because p21 leads into speech, p22 is speech only, and p23 holds the verb of saying. Kept mother's line short and bare.

items.english: "That's so," the man said, lifting his eyes.
"It comes to only three years, doesn't it. And yet we have had a good deal of hardship," he said.
notes: Kept 'only three years' in husband's plain wording, distinct from wife's refrain, and 'hardship' plain without elevation.

items.english: "Truly," she said, and again she lowered her eyes to try to see that picture. But at once, her eyes shining as if she must tell him of something great, something she herself did not understand and yet something great, "But it is only three years yet, you know."
notes: Grouped p26-p27 as one English paragraph because p26 breaks off mid-sentence into p27 speech. Kept wife's refrain as 'only three years' and eye-shining hope inarticulate, without explaining what the hope is.

data.say: Drafted the p19-p27 return to dialogue, keeping the silence, the far picture, and the three-years refrain literal.
